measurements.note: identical commits; only the interpreter and its installed distributions differ

why: A capability is not the adapter file.  It is the adapter PLUS the software that adapter calls,
and nothing in this repository stated that second half in a form a gate could check: the live
registry's `source` block is human prose ('python stdlib ast/pytest + git'), and
`declared_dependency_executables` is empty for all 419 verified capabilities.  Measured on a
clean checkout of this branch: the 22-task hardcore-SE probe reads 14/22 pass with no venv and
22/22 pass with one.  The same commit, the same code, eight capabilities appearing and
disappearing -- because the toolchain they need was never declared, so nothing could install it
and nothing could warn that it was missing.
Every entry below was attributed BY MEASUREMENT, not by reading the source: the module was
blocked with an import hook and the 22-task probe re-run, so `blocks` lists exactly the tasks
that fail when that module is absent (execution_guard/toolchain_preflight_v1.py --attribute).
why_capability_tools: A shared adapter serves several verbs (toolchain_v1 runs ruff, mypy, bandit, coverage and
crosshair), so reading the TOOLS out of the source attributes the UNION to every verb that
uses it -- which would make ruff_format demand mypy.  This map is per capability and each row
was measured: the verb failed on a bare interpreter with TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED naming that tool,
or with a suite that could not run because pytest was absent.

An empty row is a claim as well: it says this capability invokes no external tool, and it must be stated, because the fallback (read the tools out of the adapter) attributes the union of a shared adapter to every verb that uses it.
